rt:
Classify this reporter's-transcript page by its visible function. Return JSON with page_type set to exactly one supported Basic RT label.

RT_cover: a transcript title or cover page identifying the court, case, proceeding, date, reporter or volume; a caption alone on a dialogue page does not make it a cover.
RT_index: a table of contents or index of proceedings, witnesses, examinations or exhibits, usually arranged as entries with page references; quoted speaker names in an index are not dialogue.
RT_body: substantive hearing dialogue, including appearances, the court calling the matter, argument, testimony, objections, rulings and adjournment. Speaker turns or Q/A within a proceeding are strong clues.
RT_certificate: a reporter's certification or attestation of transcript accuracy, commonly with certification language and a signature; do not treat this as hearing dialogue merely because it names the proceeding or its date.
RT_other: reporter-transcript material that does not fit the categories above.

Do not output hearing-first-page markers at this stage. Advanced separately checks hearing starts. To tailor this task, add local transcript conventions, speaker designations, index layouts and certification headings. Keep these structural labels unchanged.
ct:
Classify this clerk's-transcript page by the source document's function and structure, not its topic alone. Return JSON with page_type set to exactly one supported Basic CT label.

CT_cover: a record, volume or transcript cover identifying the court, case and compilation. A repeated pleading caption is not itself a record cover.
CT_index: a compilation's table of contents or document index with entries and page references.
CT_minute_order: the court's record of a proceeding or its actual minute orders, often identifying the judicial officer, hearing date, appearances and orders made. Distinguish a court's adopted orders from requested or proposed orders.
CT_report: an authored report presenting investigation, evaluation, observations, findings or recommendations. Follow its narrative structure across continuation pages. Recommendations within a report do not make it a court order.
CT_form: a structured court form, often with labeled fields, checkboxes, a form number and printed instructions. Use this for form documents not better identified by a specific functional category below. An incidental form reference does not make a narrative report a form.
CT_certificate: a clerk's or other official certification or attestation, commonly certifying the record or copies; distinguish it from proof that a document was served.
CT_motion: a motion or application requesting judicial relief and its supporting argument. A request for an order is not an order already made.
CT_notice: a notice announcing an event, hearing, filing or action, rather than the court's minute record of what occurred.
CT_proof_of_service: a proof, declaration or certificate documenting service, commonly identifying documents served, recipients, method, date and the server's attestation. Its function controls even when presented on a standardized form.
CT_other: material that does not fit the categories above.

Classify the page actually shown: a separately identifiable attachment may be a form or proof of service rather than part of the preceding report. A report's proposed findings remain report content unless the page establishes a different document. Basic does not add first-page markers. To tailor this task, add the report types, local order headings, forms and document conventions encountered in your field, including common look-alikes. Retain the application labels; approved report/form names belong in their naming editors.
first_hearing: Review a page already classified as hearing dialogue. Return JSON with first_page set to yes or no. A hearing usually begins when the court calls the case or announces the proceeding, often followed by appearances. Consider the opening language and transcript structure together. A repeated case caption, a new speaker, a new witness, a changed topic, or a printed page number alone does not establish a new hearing. A continuation or resumption within the same hearing is not automatically a new start. Covers, indexes and certificates are not hearing starts. The application, not this response, adds RT_body_first_page for a yes answer. To tailor this task, describe customary call-of-case language, appearance sequences and distinct-session conventions in your courts.
first_minute: Review a page already classified as a minute order. Return JSON with first_page set to yes or no. Look for the start of the order: its heading, proceeding date, identifying information and first-page indicators such as Page 1 of X. Continued findings, attached order text and repeated headers belong to the same order unless the source establishes a new order. A changed issue or a repeated date alone is not enough. The application adds CT_minute_order_first_page for a yes answer. To tailor this task, describe local minute-order layouts, first-page headings and continuation conventions.
first_form: Review a page already classified as a form. Return JSON with first_page set to yes or no. Identify the beginning from the form title, initial identifying fields, form code and first-page indicators such as Page 1 of X. A form code or caption repeated on every page does not make each page a new form. Distinguish a new form from continuation sheets and attachments belonging to the same form. The application adds CT_form_first_page for a yes answer. To tailor this task, add common form layouts and start-versus-continuation clues. Put approved titles and required form codes in Form naming instructions.
date_hearing: Extract the date of the hearing from its first dialogue page. Return JSON with date as a long-form U.S. date, for example January 2, 2026, or an empty string if unresolved. Prefer the date identifying the current proceeding, often in the opening heading or the court's announcement. Do not substitute a filing, printing, certification or footer date, a past event discussed in testimony, or a future hearing setting. Resolve competing dates only from explicit source context; do not guess. To tailor this task, describe local date placement and recurring misleading dates without changing the response format.
date_minute: Extract the date of the proceeding or judicial minute order identified on its first page. Return JSON with date as a long-form U.S. date, for example January 2, 2026, or an empty string if unresolved. Distinguish the relevant hearing or order date from filing/service stamps, printing dates, attached documents' dates and future hearing settings. A date in the orders' narrative may describe another event. Use explicit source context to resolve competing dates; otherwise leave the value empty. To tailor this task, describe the local minute-order headings and date fields that identify the relevant proceeding.
